title: Contextual Restore Workbench — personal sketch
content:
Quick brain-dump for a lightweight "Contextual Restore Workbench" feature — rough PRD / user stories / engineering notes. Intended as a personal sketch to iterate with product + DX before formal PRD.

Goal / problem statement:
- Many customers want fast recovery from accidental page reloads, multi-tab workflows, or to transfer a conversation state between devices without re-running large prompt prefixes.
- Current options: full session KV caching (server-side) or client keep-alive; both have drawbacks (cost, data residency, fragility). 
- Goal: autosave condensed session deltas + metadata and provide a simple restore UX + small API that can rehydrate conversation context on demand with predictable cost and privacy controls.

Core ideas (high level):
- Session snapshot = metadata + compact delta bundle (not full prompt). Delta bundle contains: pointers to original system prompt id, short embeddings summary (optional), recent N messages (configurable), and stable KV checkpoint tokens for model cache reuse.
- Storage: short-lived (default 7 days) encrypted snapshots stored in customer-scoped object store (hosted) or a pointer to customer's S3/Vault for Private/Dedicated.
- Restore flow: client calls /sessions/restore (or clicks UI chip). Server validates permissions, fetches snapshot, rehydrates minimal state (rebuilds KV cache pointers, injects compacted messages as warm-start).
- Cost model: aim to add <5% token overhead vs naive re-send of history for typical convo lengths. For large histories, delta avoids replaying entire prefix.

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I can click "Restore" when returning to a conversation to pick up where I left off without re-sending 5k tokens of context. Acceptance: perceived latency < 300ms for UI restore, server-side warm-up < 1s for most workloads.
- As an end-user, I can share a restore link with a teammate (if tenant allows) that rehydrates the view but masks PII. Acceptance: link grants read-only reconstructed context; mask-sensitive spans.
- As an SRE, I can inspect restore-success-rate and cache-hit-rate in Redwood Console for each customer.

Rough product surface / UX notes:
- Small "Autosaved" badge in conversation header with timestamp + "Restore" action. Also a dropdown of snapshots with labels ("Today 11:04 — quick notes").
- Quick diff view: show condensed timeline (3–5 messages each side) and indicate omitted sections with "... omitted 2.2k tokens". Option to expand full replay (expensive).
- Share button: produces short-lived tokenized URL (configurable TTL) or tenant-level toggle to disallow sharing.

API sketches (brainstorm):
- POST /v1/snapshots (create) { session_id, retention_days?, mode: "auto"|"manual", redact: true|false } -> snapshot_id
- GET /v1/snapshots/{id} -> metadata + small preview
- POST /v1/sessions/restore { snapshot_id, target_session_id?, restore_mode: "warm"|"replay" } -> job_id / direct result
- Query params: include_kv_cache=true to attempt KV reuse (best-effort)

Engineering notes / implementation options:
- Encoding: delta as newline-delimited small JSON lines + optional compressed blob. Use lightweight prefix-hashing to avoid re-sending unchanged system prompts.
- Rehydration strategies: 1) synthesize short system message + recent messages (cheap), 2) full replay (expensive). Default to strategy 1, fall back to 2 on failure.
- KV cache reuse: snapshots contain cache-checksum + model-variant tag; runtime attempts to mount compatible cache shards to avoid cold-start tokens. If incompatible, record mismatch and fall back.
- Security: snapshots encrypted at rest with tenant KMS. Access controlled by API token scopes. Sharing creates scoped token with limited scope & ttl.

Metrics to track (initial):
- snapshot-created-per-customer/day
- restore-success-rate (success, partial, failed)
- avg-restore-latency-ui
- avg-additional-tokens-sent-on-restore
- cost-delta-per-restore (estimated)
- number-of-shared-snapshots (security hazard signal)

Rollout / experiment plan (sketch):
- Phase 0 (internal): implement API + runtime proof-of-concept, add lightweight UI to Redwood internal org, track metrics. Target: 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta opt-in): enable for select hosted customers + Dedicated as feature flag; collect feedback on restore correctness and cost. A/B test: "restore" vs baseline (replay history).
- Phase 2 (gradual): enable autosave default for small orgs, remain opt-in for large enterprise until compliance checks done.

Open questions / TODOs (lots):
- What is the canonical representation of "compacted" context? Do we use embeddings + retrieval stub or partial message list?
- How to robustly mask PII in shared snapshots? Post-process with redact pipeline or require upstream app redaction?
- Pricing: free with quotas? bill per-snapshot storage and per-restore token-equivalent? Need pricing input from finance.
- Edge-case: long-running sessions that rely on external tool outputs (files, tools) — snapshots may need pointers rather than inline content. Design doc for tools-in-snapshots.

Notes to self / quick action items:
- Talk to Kai about KV cache feasibility across model variants (INF-4821).
- Ask Priya to mock minimal UI (badge + snapshot dropdown) for demo next week.
- Draft Confluence page: ctx-restore-v1 (include security checklist).
- Small spike: implement snapshot create + restore on local dev cluster + metric hooks.

Rough acceptance criteria for MVP:
- create + restore flow works end-to-end for hosted API with small (<1k token) snapshots; restores succeed 95% of the time within SLA; KV reuse attempted and recorded.
- Console exposes per-tenant restore metrics and snapshot listing.
- Security controls: encryption at rest and tenant scoping; sharing disabled by default.

Unresolved UX trade-offs (opinionated):
- default retention 7d is reasonable, but allow org-level override (30d/never) for power-users. Enterprise should require explicit opt-in for long retention.
- showing omitted token counts helps set expectations but might expose info ("omitted 12k tokens") — consider fuzzy buckets.

Endnotes:
- This is messy. Need to pair with DEX + SRE + Security to tighten. Main risk: naive restore becomes a privacy / cost sink. Prioritize instrumentation.

-- Miles
